skill.name: pydicom
skill.description: Guides Python developers through DICOM file reading, metadata inspection, pixel data conversion, anonymization, and transfer syntax handling with pydicom.
skill.summary: Use pydicom workflows to inspect, convert, anonymize, and process DICOM medical imaging files.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts were false positives from Markdown backticks, pydicom documentation links, and DICOM terminology. The real risks are local file output and DICOM privacy handling: metadata exports can expose PHI, and the anonymizer is not a complete de-identification workflow.

remediation.suggestion: Redact patient, institution, physician, accession, and private tags by default. Require an explicit include-sensitive option for full exports.
Implement a DICOM de-identification profile, remove private tags, regenerate UIDs with a study-level mapping, and document pixel burn-in review.
Refuse existing output files unless a force option is supplied. Resolve paths before writing metadata output.
Pin optional package versions or tell users to install from trusted indexes in a managed Python environment.

semantic_findings.title: DICOM Metadata Export Can Expose PHI
semantic_findings.description: The metadata extractor includes patient identifiers and other DICOM elements in text or JSON output. Exporting this output without redaction can disclose protected health information.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code explicitly reads PatientName, PatientID, birth date, and all non-sequence dataset elements, then writes or prints the result. DICOM metadata commonly contains PHI.

semantic_findings.title: Anonymization Does Not Fully De-Identify DICOM Data
semantic_findings.description: The anonymizer removes a fixed list of tags but leaves UID regeneration commented out and preserves pixel data. Users could share files that still contain indirect identifiers or burned-in annotations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script targets common PHI tags but does not apply a full DICOM de-identification profile. The source comments show UID anonymization is optional and disabled by default.

content.user_title: Process DICOM Medical Images with pydicom
content.value_statement: DICOM workflows often require careful metadata, pixel, and privacy handling. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical pydicom guidance for medical imaging tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to read and write DICOM files with pydicom datasets.
Shows how to inspect patient, study, series, image, and file metadata.
Provides a script for converting DICOM pixel data to common image formats.
Provides a script for removing common PHI tags from DICOM files.
Documents transfer syntaxes, compression handlers, and decompression workflows.
Shows how to process multi-frame files and related DICOM series.
limitations: The anonymization helper is not a complete HIPAA or DICOM PS3.15 de-identification tool.
Compressed pixel data may require optional packages such as pylibjpeg, gdcm, or Pillow.
The skill does not implement PACS networking or DICOMweb clients.
Scripts process local files and can overwrite outputs when paths are chosen poorly.

use_cases.title: Review Radiology Data
use_cases.description: Inspect DICOM tags, transfer syntaxes, and image metadata before building processing scripts.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Datasets
use_cases.description: Convert scans to images and prepare metadata summaries while tracking privacy limits.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Ask for pydicom examples, helper script usage, and troubleshooting steps during AI-assisted development.
use_cases.target_user: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users

prompt_templates.title: Inspect DICOM Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this pydicom skill to explain the important tags in a DICOM file and list privacy-sensitive fields to check.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Scan Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help convert a DICOM scan to PNG with windowing. Include package requirements and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan De-Identification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a DICOM anonymization workflow for a research folder. Flag PHI risks that the helper script does not cover.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Series Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Python pipeline that reads a DICOM series, sorts slices, creates a volume, and records transfer syntax issues.

output_examples.input: Extract metadata from one DICOM file for review.
output_examples.output: A concise metadata summary with patient, study, series, image, and file meta sections, plus warnings about sensitive fields.

output_examples.input: Convert a CT image to PNG with display windowing.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step conversion plan that checks dependencies, reads pixel data, applies VOI LUT windowing, and saves an image.

output_examples.input: Prepare DICOM files for research sharing.
output_examples.output: A de-identification checklist covering common tags, UID handling, private tags, pixel annotations, and verification before release.

best_practices: Validate input files before reading pixel data from untrusted sources.
Redact or review PHI before saving metadata outside a protected environment.
Install optional compression handlers only in managed Python environments.
anti_patterns: Do not treat sample anonymization as regulatory compliance.
Do not export full metadata into shared locations without review.
Do not assume every compressed scan can be decoded without extra packages.

faq.question: Does this skill install pydicom for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and guidance, but installation must be approved and run in your environment.

faq.question: Can it anonymize DICOM files safely?
faq.answer: It can help remove common identifiers, but you must verify de-identification against your policy and DICOM standards.

faq.question: Can it convert scans to PNG or JPEG?
faq.answer: Yes. The included guidance and script cover common image conversion workflows with optional windowing.

faq.question: Does it support compressed DICOM files?
faq.answer: Yes, with optional handlers for JPEG, JPEG 2000, JPEG-LS, RLE, and related transfer syntaxes.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code assisted development workflows.

faq.question: Does it connect to PACS systems?
faq.answer: No. It explains PACS context but does not include DICOM networking tools.
